Hunting is purely entertainment; Roosevelt's conservation arguments stand independent of his personal sport interests
Conservation requires absolute exclusion of human use; Roosevelt was simply mistaken about the role of hunter activity
Modern conservation has moved beyond Roosevelt; his writings have no current relevance to wildlife management today
context: Roosevelt argued, and the North American Model embodied, that sportsmen who fund and respect regulated harvest are the most effective conservationists. The contradiction critics see (kill animals / save species) dissolves at the population level. African Game Trails (1910), The Wilderness Hunter (1893).

question: The Order of Crocodilia survived the K-Pg extinction (66 mya) that ended non-avian dinosaurs. The order's body plan dates to the Triassic — over 200 million years stable. Why does this 'success' belie any simple notion of evolutionary progress?
answer: Stability and persistence can be evolutionary success without morphological complexification — the crocodile body plan is well-adapted, not 'primitive'
choices: Stability and persistence can be evolutionary success without morphological complexification — the crocodile body plan is well-adapted, not 'primitive'
Crocodiles are simply unevolved — their stability reflects an absence of selection pressure rather than a successful adaptation
Crocodiles' stability shows that evolution always tends toward conservative forms — change is the exception, not the rule, in biology
Crocodiles evolved most recently from other reptiles — the apparent stability of body plan masks rapid contemporary evolution at every level
context: Crocodilian persistence — semi-aquatic ambush predator body plan stable across ~200 million years — is real evolutionary success. Stable doesn't mean primitive; it means well-tuned to a stable niche. The 'evolutionary progress' framing (lower-to-higher) is largely abandoned in modern biology. Gould, Conway Morris, others on contingency vs convergence.

question: Antarctic and Arctic conditions both freeze water — but only the Arctic has freeze-tolerant frogs (wood frog, chorus frog, spring peeper) as native fauna. Antarctica has none. Why?
answer: Glacial history — Antarctic glaciation cleared terrestrial amphibians before tolerance could evolve in any frog lineage
choices: Glacial history — Antarctic glaciation cleared terrestrial amphibians before tolerance could evolve in any frog lineage
Climate severity — Antarctica is too cold for any freeze-tolerant adaptation, while Arctic temperatures sit within range
Habitat type — Antarctica simply lacks breeding ponds frogs require, making freeze tolerance unnecessary on the continent
Marine isolation — Antarctica's surrounding sea is too cold for amphibian larval dispersal across the southern oceans
context: Antarctica's glaciation history is the key. Continental ice sheets stripped Antarctica of terrestrial fauna before amphibian freeze-tolerance could evolve. Arctic regions had glacial-interglacial cycles, allowing refugia and re-colonization. Biogeographic contingency shapes which adaptations exist where.

question: Snake venom complexity varies enormously — over 100 different toxin families across snake families. Yet within one species, venom composition can vary by geographic location, age, and even diet. What does this within-species variation suggest?
answer: Venom is under ongoing selection by local prey availability — populations adapt venom to local prey biochemistry across short evolutionary timescales
choices: Venom is under ongoing selection by local prey availability — populations adapt venom to local prey biochemistry across short evolutionary timescales
Venom variation is purely genetic drift — snake venom composition has no functional consequence at the level of individual variation
Venom is determined by climate — cold-adapted populations produce neurotoxic venom; warm-adapted populations produce hemotoxic venom
Venom complexity is fixed at the species level — within-population variation reflects measurement error rather than real variation
context: Daltry et al. (1996) and later work showed snake venom composition tracks local prey assemblies — diet drives selection on venom proteins. Within-species variation in venom is functional, not noise. This complicates antivenom production (one regional venom may not match another's) and explains why venom evolution is so rapid. Adaptive variation in real time.
